sections.title: Design Specification
sections.content:
**Overview**

Group resolved references of a source file into usage entries by definition target, filtering out self-references and providing context around usage locations for downstream output.

- Call `build_callee_usages()` to collect references from this file that target other files, grouped by target file and definition with context text from the target file.
- Call `build_same_file_usages()` to collect references from this file that target its own definitions, grouped by name and target definition, excluding references written inside the definition's own lines.
- Call `build_caller_usages()` to collect references from other files that target definitions in this file, grouped by caller and definition name with surrounding source context.

This file depends on definition extraction (`DefinitionInfo`, `extract_definitions()`), reference resolution (`reference_target_list()`, `ReferenceTarget` union type, `reference_kind()`), source text access (`read_source()`, `line_list_of()`, `parse_file()`), and language-specific definition lookup (`find_definition()`, `source_definition()`, `r_definition_list()`) to build usage summaries. It is used by `codetwine/file_analyzer.py` to populate usage fields in file analysis output, receiving resolved references and definitions as input and returning grouped usage dictionaries keyed by line ranges, names, and target metadata.

Memoization via `_memo_definition_function()` ensures each unique reference target's definition is looked up only once per analysis, reducing redundant file I/O and definition searches. Same-file references written inside the definition they name are automatically filtered using line range checks (`own_range_list`) to exclude self-references and recursive calls. Definition context is retrieved differently per language via `_TARGET_DEFINITION_FUNCTION_DICT`: COBOL uses parsed source, R uses line ranges of top-level assignments, C# and import languages use syntax-tree-based definition lookup.

**Definitions**

## `_TargetDefinition`

A frozen dataclass holding the definition a reference resolves to for use in usage entries: source text of the definition, the name it is listed under in the target file, and its starting line number; all three are None when a reference has no definition or the definition is not found.

## `_NO_DEFINITION`

A sentinel `_TargetDefinition` instance with all fields None, returned when a reference target has no definition or the definition cannot be resolved.

## `_memo_definition_function`

Return a function that caches definition lookups by reference target fields other than line, so each distinct target is looked up once; used internally to avoid redundant definition searches during reference grouping.

## `_group_other_file_target_list`

Group references that resolve to files other than the current file by target file, reference name, and definition, collecting line numbers into a sorted set for each group and returning one dict per group with target definition context and metadata.

## `_definition_range_dict`

Build a dictionary mapping definition names to lists of (start_line, end_line) tuples from a definition list, used to look up line ranges of definitions during same-file reference filtering.

## `_cobol_own_range_function`

Return a function giving the line range of the definition a COBOL reference target names, or an empty list if the target has no definition, for use in filtering self-references.

## `_r_own_range_function`

Return a function giving the line ranges of top-level (non-member, non-attach) definitions matching the name of an R reference target, handling R's scoping where a usage root name may correspond to multiple definitions.

## `_name_own_range_function`

Return a function giving the line range of the definition that a C# or import reference target names: if the name has multiple parts (e.g., `Cfg.Max`), the range of the member definition matching the last part; otherwise the range of definitions matching the first part of the written name or definition name, used to identify and exclude self-references in C# and import-based languages.

## `_OWN_RANGE_FUNCTION_DICT`

A module-level dictionary mapping reference kind strings ("cobol", "r", "csharp", "import") to functions that return line ranges of definitions a same-file reference names, used during same-file usage grouping to filter out self-references.

## `TREE_RANGE_KIND_SET`

A module-level set of reference kind strings ("r") whose own-range functions require parsing the syntax tree (root_node), used by callers to determine whether to parse a file's AST before calling `build_same_file_usages()`.

## `_group_same_file_target_list`

Group references that resolve to definitions in the same file by name and target definition, filtering out references written inside the definition's own line range (self-references, recursive calls), and returning one dict per group with line numbers, names, and target definition metadata.

## `_cobol_definition_function`

Return a function that resolves a COBOL reference target to its definition as a `_TargetDefinition`, reading the target file and extracting definition text via `parse_file()` and the COBOL source's `definition_text()` method.

## `_r_definition_function`

Return a function that resolves an R reference target to its definition as a `_TargetDefinition`, extracting definition source by reading the target file once and slicing it from start_line to end_line, with memoized file access to avoid re-reading.

## `_csharp_definition_function`

Return a function that resolves a C# reference target to its declaration via `_source_target_definition()`, looking up the definition named by the target's definition_name on the target's definition_line.

## `_import_definition_function`

Return a function that resolves an import reference target to the definition named by its definition_name via `_source_target_definition()`, supporting languages resolved through import statements.

## `_source_target_definition`

Look up a definition by name and optional start_line using `source_definition()`, returning a `_TargetDefinition` with the definition text and metadata, or `_NO_DEFINITION` when the definition is not found or the file does not support syntax-tree definition extraction.

## `_TARGET_DEFINITION_FUNCTION_DICT`

A module-level dictionary mapping reference kind strings ("cobol", "r", "csharp", "import") to functions that return definition lookup functions for those languages, used to retrieve target definitions during usage grouping.

## `build_callee_usages`

Build a list of caller usage entries for a file by grouping its references that resolve to other files by target file, name, and definition; return empty list if the file has no language; used to populate callee_usages in file analysis output.

## `build_same_file_usages`

Build a list of same-file usage entries by grouping references that resolve to the file's own definitions, filtering out references inside the definition's line range, and sorting line numbers; returns empty list if the file has no language or if root_node is required but not provided; used to populate same_file_usages in file analysis output.

## `_group_caller_usage_list`

Group a single caller file's references that resolve to a target file by reference name and target definition, returning a dict mapping (name, definition_name, definition_start_line) tuples to usage groups with sorted, deduplicated line numbers, used internally by `build_caller_usages()`.

## `_attach_usage_context`

Add a `usage_context` field to each group dict from `_group_caller_usage_list()` by extracting up to `_MAX_CONTEXT_LOCATION` lines from the caller file with `_CONTEXT_RADIUS` lines of surrounding code, joined by "\n...\n"; does nothing if the file cannot be read or is empty, used to provide code context in caller usage output.

## `build_caller_usages`

Build a list of caller usage entries for a target file by collecting and resolving references from each caller file that depend on it, grouping by name and definition, and attaching usage context; returns empty list if no callers depend on the file; used to populate caller_usages in file analysis output showing where definitions are used.

summary:
# Summary: codetwine/extractors/usage_analysis.py

**Responsibility:** Groups resolved references into usage entries by target definition, filtering self-references and providing context for downstream output.

**Main Public Functions:**
- `build_callee_usages()` – groups references targeting other files
- `build_same_file_usages()` – groups same-file references, excluding self-references
- `build_caller_usages()` – groups references from callers to this file's definitions

**Key Concepts:** Usage grouping by target file and definition name, self-reference filtering via line ranges, definition context extraction per language (COBOL, R, C#, import), memoized definition lookup to reduce redundant I/O, usage context from surrounding source code.
